subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3(a)–(b) of the parent proof (localisation at a good radius; Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2 with the slice estimate 4.9–4.11). The parent works with μ = μ_j and t ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1) and intersects with V to make the measures finite. Here the hypothesis that μ is finite on every ball does that job, so the argument covers every t ∈ ℝ.

Notation. B_s := ball(0, s) and B̄_s := closedBall(0, s) (both empty for s < 0). |x| is the Euclidean norm. For t, h ∈ ℝ put S(t, h) := {x : t − h < |x| < t}, A(t, h) := μ(S(t, h)) and f(t, h) := ofReal(h⁻¹)·A(t, h) ∈ [0, ∞]. Then D(t) = liminf_{h→0+} f(t, h), the liminf along 𝓝[>]0 in the complete lattice [0, ∞].

1. (Sets.) Let h > 0 and t ∈ ℝ. Then S(t, h) = B_t ∖ B̄_{t−h}: |x| < t means x ∈ B_t, and t − h < |x| means x ∉ B̄_{t−h}. Moreover B̄_{t−h} ⊆ B_t because t − h < t (closedBall_subset_ball).
2. (Differences.) Let h > 0. B̄_{t−h} is closed, hence measurable, and μ(B̄_{t−h}) ≤ μ(B_t) < ∞ by step 1 and the hypothesis. By measure_sdiff (the current name of measure_diff at this Mathlib pin), A(t, h) = μ(B_t) − μ(B̄_{t−h}) (truncated subtraction in [0, ∞]).
3. (Measurability in t for fixed h > 0.) F(s) := μ(B_s) and G(s) := μ(B̄_s) are monotone functions ℝ → [0, ∞] (ball_subset_ball, closedBall_subset_closedBall, measure_mono), so they are Borel measurable (Monotone.measurable). Hence t ↦ G(t − h) is measurable (composition with the measurable map t ↦ t − h). Subtraction on [0, ∞] is measurable (instance MeasurableSub₂ ℝ≥0∞, Measurable.sub). By step 2, t ↦ A(t, h) = F(t) − G(t − h) is measurable, and so is t ↦ f(t, h) (Measurable.const_mul).
4. (Monotonicity in h.) If 0 < h' ≤ h then S(t, h') ⊆ S(t, h), because t − h ≤ t − h'. Hence A(t, h') ≤ A(t, h) (measure_mono).
5. (Liminf as a sup of infima.) The filter 𝓝[>]0 on ℝ has the basis {Ioo(0, ε) : ε > 0} (nhdsGT_basis 0). By Filter.HasBasis.liminf_eq_iSup_iInf, D(t) = ⨆_{ε>0} I_ε(t) with I_ε(t) := ⨅_{h ∈ (0, ε)} f(t, h). If ε ≤ ε' then I_{ε'}(t) ≤ I_ε(t), since the infimum runs over a larger set. For every ε > 0 there is k ∈ ℕ with 1/(k + 1) < ε (exists_nat_one_div_lt). Hence D(t) = ⨆_{k∈ℕ} I_{1/(k+1)}(t). Indeed "≥" holds because 1/(k + 1) > 0, and "≤" holds because I_ε(t) ≤ I_{1/(k+1)}(t) whenever 1/(k + 1) ≤ ε.
6. (Rational infima; the rational approximation of the parent's step 3(b).) Fix ε > 0 and t, and let J_ε(t) := ⨅ {f(t, q) : q ∈ ℚ, 0 < q < ε}. Every such q is a real number in (0, ε), so I_ε(t) ≤ J_ε(t). For the converse fix h ∈ (0, ε). Put a := A(t, h). Then a ≤ μ(B_t) < ∞, since S(t, h) ⊆ B_t. The map x ↦ ofReal(x⁻¹)·a is continuous at x = h: x ↦ x⁻¹ is continuous at h ≠ 0 (tendsto_inv₀), ofReal is continuous, and multiplication by the finite constant a is continuous (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const). Let c > f(t, h) = ofReal(h⁻¹)·a. Then ofReal(x⁻¹)·a < c for all x in some interval (l, h) with l < h (Tendsto.eventually_lt_const along 𝓝[<]h, then mem_nhdsLT_iff_exists_Ioo_subset). Choose a rational q with max(l, 0) < q < h (exists_rat_btwn). Then 0 < q < h < ε, and A(t, q) ≤ A(t, h) = a by step 4. So J_ε(t) ≤ f(t, q) = ofReal(q⁻¹)·A(t, q) ≤ ofReal(q⁻¹)·a < c. Since c > f(t, h) was arbitrary, J_ε(t) ≤ f(t, h) (le_of_forall_gt). Taking the infimum over h ∈ (0, ε) gives J_ε(t) ≤ I_ε(t), hence I_ε(t) = J_ε(t). (Equivalently, as in the parent: a rational h' ∈ [h/(1 + δ), h] has h'⁻¹A(t, h') ≤ (1 + δ)h⁻¹A(t, h), and δ → 0.)
7. (Conclusion.) By steps 5 and 6, D(t) = ⨆_{k∈ℕ} ⨅_{q ∈ Q_k} f(t, q) for every t ∈ ℝ, where Q_k := {q ∈ ℚ : 0 < q ∧ q < 1/(k + 1)}, a countable index type (a subtype of ℚ). For q ∈ Q_k we have q > 0, so t ↦ f(t, q) is measurable by step 3. A countable infimum and a countable supremum of measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions are measurable (Measurable.iInf with the countable type Q_k, then Measurable.iSup over ℕ). Hence D is measurable. ∎

Source: steps 3(c) and 4 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2, chapter-06.txt lines 2090–2100, with 4.10 at line 1374: a good slicing radius chosen via the integrated slice bound 4.10 and an argument as in Ch. 2, 6.7(2)), stated for an abstract sequence of measures μ_j. Notation. |x| is the Euclidean norm and B_s := ball(0, s). For t ∈ ℝ, D_j(t) := liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_j({x : t − h < |x| < t}), the liminf along 𝓝[>]0 in [0, ∞]. Let ν be Lebesgue measure on ℝ restricted to (r₀, r₀ + 1).

1. (Measurability.) For each j, D_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] is Borel measurable. This is (DM) applied to μ_j; its hypothesis μ_j(B_r) < ∞ for every r ∈ ℝ is part of ours.
2. (Integral bound, 4.10.) Fix j. Apply (SI) with μ := μ_j, f := |·| (continuous, hence measurable), W := ℝ^P (MeasurableSet.univ), L := 1, m := D_j and (a, b) := (r₀, r₀ + 1). Its pointwise hypothesis holds with equality: for t ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1) and every h, ℝ^P ∩ {t − h < |x| < t} = {t − h < |x| < t} (univ_inter), and 1·liminf(…) = D_j(t) (one_mul). Hence ∫⁻_{(r₀, r₀+1)} D_j(t) dt ≤ 1·μ_j(ℝ^P ∩ {r₀ < |x| < r₀ + 1}). The set {r₀ < |x| < r₀ + 1} lies in B_{r₀+1}, so by measure_mono and the hypothesis, ∫⁻ D_j dν ≤ μ_j(B_{r₀+1}) ≤ Λ₀.
3. (Fatou.) Put G(t) := liminf_{j→∞} D_j(t) ∈ [0, ∞]. G is measurable (Measurable.liminf with step 1). By Fatou's lemma (lintegral_liminf_le with step 1), ∫⁻ G dν ≤ liminf_j ∫⁻ D_j dν. Every term of this sequence is ≤ Λ₀ by step 2, so the liminf is ≤ Λ₀ (liminf_le_of_frequently_le'). Hence ∫⁻ G dν ≤ Λ₀ < ∞.
4. (A good radius.) By ae_lt_top (G measurable, ∫⁻ G dν ≠ ∞), G(t) < ∞ for ν-a.e. t. By ae_restrict_iff' (measurableSet_Ioo), for Lebesgue-a.e. t, t ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1) implies G(t) < ∞. Suppose G(t) = ∞ for every t ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1). Then (r₀, r₀ + 1) is contained in the Lebesgue null set {t : ¬(t ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1) → G(t) < ∞)}, which contradicts volume((r₀, r₀ + 1)) = 1 ≠ 0 (measure_mono_null, Real.volume_Ioo). So there is t₀ ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1) with G(t₀) < ∞.
5. (Subsequence.) Put C := G(t₀).toNNReal + 1 ∈ [0, ∞). Since G(t₀) < ∞, G(t₀) = ↑(G(t₀).toNNReal) < ↑C (ENNReal.coe_toNNReal). So liminf_j D_j(t₀) < C, and by Filter.frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt, D_j(t₀) < C for frequently many j in atTop. By Filter.extraction_of_frequently_atTop there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with D_{φ(j)}(t₀) < C for every j. In particular D_{φ(j)}(t₀) ≤ C for every j. ∎

Then there are T′ ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R′ in U with R′.Represents T′, R′.carrier = M ∩ E, R′.mult = θ and R′.orient = ξ, such that: (i) R′.measure = R.measure⌞E, i.e. θHⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) = (θHⁿ⌞M)⌞E; (ii) T′(ω) = T(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ E; (iii) T′(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose tsupport is disjoint from E.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U E : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet E → R.Represents T → ∃ (T' : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R' : IMRep U n), R'.Represents T' ∧ R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E ∧ R'.mult = R.mult ∧ R'.orient = R.orient ∧ R'.measure = R.measure.restrict E ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ E → T' ω = T ω) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) E → T' ω = 0

Source: steps 5–8 of the parent proof (T'_j := T_{φ(j)}⌞B_{t₀}, built by restricting the representation; agreement on forms supported in W; vanishing off B_{t₀}, used for the support; weight μ⌞B, used for the mass). Here they are stated for an arbitrary Borel set E in place of B_{t₀}. The parent uses E = B_{t₀} and U = ℝ^P.
Siblings used: (IC) cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, part (b).

Notation. R = (M, θ, ξ), i.e. M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient; Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For a test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (also used for the underlying form) put F_ω(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) ∈ ℝ. If ω(x) = 0 then F_ω(x) = 0, since ξ(x) is linear (map_zero).

1. (Construction.) U is open and E is measurable, so (IC)(b) applied to R and E gives T' ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R' in U with R'.Represents T', R'.carrier = M ∩ E, R'.mult = θ and R'.orient = ξ. These are the first four conclusions.
2. (Formulas.) By IMRep.Represents and IMRep.action, for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U): T'(ω) = ∫_{M∩E} F_ω dHⁿ (using the three equalities of step 1) and T(ω) = ∫_M F_ω dHⁿ.
3. (Weight.) By definition, R'.measure = (Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)).withDensity θ and R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ, with θ read in [0, ∞]. Since E is measurable, restrict_withDensity gives R.measure⌞E = ((Hⁿ⌞M)⌞E).withDensity θ, and Measure.restrict_restrict gives (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞E = Hⁿ⌞(E ∩ M) = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) (inter_comm). Hence R'.measure = R.measure⌞E.
4. (Agreement.) Let tsupport ω ⊆ E. If x ∈ M ∖ E, then x ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and F_ω(x) = 0. M is measurable (R.measurableSet_carrier) and M ∩ E ⊆ M. Since F_ω vanishes on M ∖ (M ∩ E) = M ∖ E, setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero gives ∫_M F_ω dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩E} F_ω dHⁿ (its deprecated alias is setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_diff_eq_zero). By step 2, T'(ω) = T(ω).
5. (Vanishing.) Let tsupport ω be disjoint from E. If x ∈ M ∩ E, then x ∉ tsupport ω, so F_ω(x) = 0. By setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero and step 2, T'(ω) = ∫_{M∩E} F_ω dHⁿ = 0. ∎

subproblems.title: Evaluation bound |T(ω)| ≤ ∫ |ω| dμ_T for an integer multiplicity current (parent step 9(d))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep in U representing T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n). Then ofReal|T(ω)| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(|ω(x)|) dμ_R(x), where μ_R := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), R.Represents T → ENNReal.ofReal |T ω| ≤ ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x)) ∂R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 9(d) of the parent proof ("|T(dg_h ∧ η)| = |∫⟨dg_h ∧ η, ξ⟩ dμ| ≤ ∫|dg_h ∧ η| dμ", using step 2: |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x). This is the estimate behind Simon Ch. 6, 4.11, where M(T⌞A) = μ_T(A). Here it is stated for an arbitrary test form and an arbitrary domain U.
Siblings used: (IC) cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, part (d).

Notation. R = (M, θ, ξ); Hⁿ := μHE[n]; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; μ_R := R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. Put F(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)).

1. (Representation.) By IMRep.Represents and IMRep.action, T(ω) = ∫ F d(Hⁿ⌞M).
2. (Norm of an integral.) ofReal|T(ω)| = ‖T(ω)‖ₑ (Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs) ≤ ∫⁻ ‖F(x)‖ₑ d(Hⁿ⌞M)(x) (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm). This holds without integrability, since the Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0. For each x, ‖F(x)‖ₑ = ofReal|F(x)| = θ(x)·ofReal|ξ(x)(ω(x))|, because θ(x) is a natural number (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_natCast).
3. (Orientation bound.) By (IC)(d), for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α. With α = ω(x) this gives θ(x)·ofReal|ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ θ(x)·ofReal(|ω(x)|) for a.e. x. By lintegral_mono_ae, ∫⁻ ‖F‖ₑ d(Hⁿ⌞M) ≤ ∫⁻ θ(x)·ofReal(|ω(x)|) d(Hⁿ⌞M)(x).
4. (Density.) The density x ↦ (θ(x) : [0, ∞]) is measurable (R.measurable_mult composed with the cast ℕ → [0, ∞]) and finite everywhere. So lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul_non_measurable gives ∫⁻ θ·ofReal(|ω|) d(Hⁿ⌞M) = ∫⁻ ofReal(|ω|) d((Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ) = ∫⁻ ofReal(|ω(x)|) dμ_R(x). That lemma needs no measurability of the integrand. Alternatively, x ↦ ofReal(|ω(x)|) is continuous, because ω is C^∞ and α ↦ |α| is the square root of a finite sum of squares of the continuous evaluations α ↦ α(e_I). Then lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul applies.
5. (Conclusion.) Steps 1–4 give ofReal|T(ω)| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(|ω(x)|) dμ_R(x). ∎

subproblems.title: Simon's identity 4.11 for one cut-off: |T(g dη)| ≤ a·M_V(∂T) + c·μ_T(S) (parent step 9(b)–(d))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U, V, S ⊆ ℝ^P, a, c ∈ ℝ, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in U representing T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U). Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with tsupport g ⊆ V, |g(x)| ≤ a and ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ c for every x (operator norm of fderiv ℝ g x), and Dg(x) ≠ 0 only for x ∈ S. Let η ∈ 𝒟^m(U) satisfy |η(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, where |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm is the Euclidean coefficient norm. Then ofReal|R.action(g dη)| ≤ ofReal(a)·M_V(∂T) + ofReal(c)·μ_R(S). Here R.action(g dη) = ∫_M θ(x)⟨g(x)dη(x), ξ(x)⟩ dH^{m+1}(x) = T(g dη), dη = exteriorDerivative η, M_V = massOn V and μ_R = R.measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U V S : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (R : IMRep U (m + 1)) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (η : TestFormOn U m) (a c : ℝ), R.Represents T → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → tsupport g ⊆ V → (∀ x, |g x| ≤ a) → (∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖ ≤ c) → (∀ x, fderiv ℝ g x ≠ 0 → x ∈ S) → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ≤ 1) → ENNReal.ofReal |R.action (fun x => g x • exteriorDerivative (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x)| ≤ ENNReal.ofReal a * T.boundary.massOn V + ENNReal.ofReal c * R.measure S
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 9(b)–(d) of the parent proof, i.e. Simon's identity 4.11, T(g dη) = ∂T(gη) − T(dg ∧ η) (Ch. 6, chapter-06.txt lines 1378–1386), with the two estimates of 9(c) and 9(d), for a general cut-off g. The parent's bound √(m+1)|Dg||η| for |dg ∧ η| (Cauchy–Schwarz, step 9(d)) is replaced by the sharper accepted bound ‖Dg‖|η| of cmcs_wedge_norm_le. The parent's 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 is replaced by |g| ≤ a.
Siblings used: (AB) dtc_bc_lc_fd_lz_action_bound; (LB) cmcs_cd_extDeriv_smul_leibniz; (WN) cmcs_wedge_norm_le.

Notation. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; d := exteriorDerivative (Mathlib's extDeriv); Dg(x) := fderiv ℝ g x; 𝒜 := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin. A test form and its underlying form are denoted alike. μ_R := R.measure. M_V := massOn V.

0. (Preliminaries.)
 (i) ℝ^P contains 0, so a ≥ |g(0)| ≥ 0 and c ≥ ‖Dg(0)‖ ≥ 0.
 (ii) (Homogeneity.) For s ∈ ℝ and a covector α, |s·α| = |s|·|α|. Each coefficient satisfies (sα)(e_I) = s·α(e_I), so the sum of squares in covectorEuclideanNorm is multiplied by s², and √(s²Q) = |s|√Q (Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
 (iii) (Products are test forms.) Let φ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ and ζ ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Then x ↦ φ(x)ζ(x) is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul) and has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_left). Its topological support lies in tsupport ζ ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_right) and in tsupport φ (tsupport_smul_subset_left). So it is an element of 𝒟^k(U) = TestFormOn U k.
1. (Three test forms.) By 0(iii), ω₁ := gη ∈ 𝒟^m(U). Next dη := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U), whose underlying form is exteriorDerivative η, so ω₂ := g·dη ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U), again by 0(iii). Finally E := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m ω₁ − ω₂ ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U), a difference of two elements of the submodule.
2. (Leibniz rule; identity 4.11.) g is C^∞ and η is C^∞ (a test form), so both are differentiable at every x. By (LB), d(gη)(x) = g(x)·dη(x) + 𝒜((Dg(x)).smulRight(η(x))), hence E(x) = 𝒜((Dg(x)).smulRight(η(x))) for every x. T is linear, and ∂T(ω₁) = T(exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m ω₁) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply). So T(ω₂) = T(dω₁) − T(E) = ∂T(ω₁) − T(E). By R.Represents T, T(ω₂) = R.action(ω₂) = R.action(x ↦ g(x)·dη(x)), the left side of the claim. Therefore ofReal|R.action(g dη)| = ofReal|∂T(ω₁) − T(E)| ≤ ofReal|∂T(ω₁)| + ofReal|T(E)| (abs_sub, ENNReal.ofReal_add, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal).
3. (Boundary term, 9(c).) Claim: ofReal|∂T(ω₁)| ≤ ofReal(a)·M_V(∂T).
 If a = 0, then g = 0 by |g| ≤ a, so ω₁ = 0 and ∂T(ω₁) = 0.
 Let a > 0 and ζ := a⁻¹·ω₁ ∈ 𝒟^m(U). Then tsupport ζ ⊆ tsupport g ⊆ V, and |ζ(x)| = a⁻¹|g(x)|·|η(x)| ≤ a⁻¹·a·1 = 1 by 0(ii). So ζ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U m V, and so is −ζ (tsupport_neg, covectorEuclideanNorm_neg). By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ofReal(∂T(ζ)) ≤ M_V(∂T) and ofReal(−∂T(ζ)) = ofReal(∂T(−ζ)) ≤ M_V(∂T). Since |y| ∈ {y, −y} (abs_choice) and ∂T(−ζ) = −∂T(ζ) (map_neg), ofReal|∂T(ζ)| ≤ M_V(∂T). As ∂T(ω₁) = a·∂T(ζ) by linearity, ofReal|∂T(ω₁)| = ofReal(a)·ofReal|∂T(ζ)| ≤ ofReal(a)·M_V(∂T).
4. (Wedge term, 9(d).) Claim: ofReal|E(x)| ≤ 1_S(x)·ofReal(c) for every x.
 If x ∈ S: by (WN) and the hypotheses, |E(x)| = |𝒜((Dg(x)).smulRight(η(x)))| ≤ ‖Dg(x)‖·|η(x)| ≤ c·1 = c.
 If x ∉ S: then Dg(x) = 0 by hypothesis, so (Dg(x)).smulRight(η(x)) = 0, E(x) = 𝒜(0) = 0 (𝒜 is linear) and |E(x)| = 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero).
 By (AB) applied to T, R and E, and by lintegral_mono and lintegral_indicator_const_le (valid for an arbitrary set S): ofReal|T(E)| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(|E(x)|) dμ_R(x) ≤ ∫⁻ 1_S·ofReal(c) dμ_R ≤ ofReal(c)·μ_R(S).
5. (Conclusion.) Steps 2–4 give ofReal|R.action(x ↦ g(x)·dη(x))| ≤ ofReal(a)·M_V(∂T) + ofReal(c)·μ_R(S). ∎

subproblems.title: Boundary mass of the truncation T⌞B_{t₀}: M(∂(T⌞B_{t₀})) ≤ 2M_V(∂T) + 2·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_T({t₀ − h < |x| < t₀}) (parent step 9)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U, V ⊆ ℝ^P and t₀ ∈ ℝ with closedBall(0, t₀) ⊆ V. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in U representing T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U). Let R′ be an IMRep in U with carrier M ∩ B_{t₀} (B_{t₀} := ball(0, t₀)), multiplicity θ and orientation ξ, representing T′ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U). Then M(∂T′) ≤ 2·M_V(∂T) + 2·liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_R({x : t₀ − h < |x| < t₀}). Here M = mass = M_U, M_V = massOn V, μ_R = R.measure, and the liminf is along 𝓝[>]0 in [0, ∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U V : Set (Euclid P)) (T T' : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (R R' : IMRep U (m + 1)) (t₀ : ℝ), closedBall (0 : Euclid P) t₀ ⊆ V → R.Represents T → R'.Represents T' → R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ ball (0 : Euclid P) t₀ → R'.mult = R.mult → R'.orient = R.orient → T'.boundary.mass ≤ 2 * T.boundary.massOn V + 2 * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * R.measure {x : Euclid P | t₀ - h < ‖x‖ ∧ ‖x‖ < t₀}) (𝓝[>] 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the parent proof (the computation 4.11 with a radial cut-off; Simon Ch. 6, proof of 4.9, chapter-06.txt lines 1378–1402), applied to T' = T⌞B_{t₀}. One change: the cut-offs γ_h(|x|) of step 9(a) are replaced by those of the accepted sibling cmcs_level_cutoff (f = |·|, L = 1). These satisfy |g_h| ≤ 2 instead of 0 ≤ g_h ≤ 1, and ‖Dg_h‖ ≤ 1/(h(1 − h/2)) ≤ 2/h instead of c₁/h. Hence the constants 2 and 2. The limit h → 0+ (step 9(e)) is the accepted dominated-convergence sibling cmcs_smp_cutoff_integral_tendsto.
Siblings used: (CE) dtc_bc_lc_fd_lz_cutoff_estimate; (LC) cmcs_level_cutoff; (DC) cmcs_smp_cutoff_integral_tendsto; (IC) cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, part (d).

Notation. n := m + 1, Hⁿ := μHE[n], R = (M, θ, ξ), ν := Hⁿ⌞M, μ_R := R.measure, |x| the Euclidean norm, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, B_{t₀} := ball(0, t₀). Put A(h) := μ_R({x : t₀ − h < |x| < t₀}), D := liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·A(h) (along 𝓝[>]0) and N := M_V(∂T) = T.boundary.massOn V. The mass M(∂T') is T'.boundary.mass = T'.boundary.massOn U.

1. (Reduction to one test form.) T'.boundary.massOn U is the supremum of ofReal(∂T'(η)) over η ∈ massAdmissibleOn U m U, i.e. over η ∈ 𝒟^m(U) with |η(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (the support condition tsupport η ⊆ U holds for every element of TestFormOn U m). By sSup_le it suffices to show ofReal(∂T'(η)) ≤ 2N + 2D for each such η. If N = ∞ the right side is ∞. So assume N < ∞ and fix η.
2. (The limit value.) Put F(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(dη(x)), where dη = exteriorDerivative η. By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, R'.Represents T' and R'.carrier = M ∩ B_{t₀}, R'.mult = θ, R'.orient = ξ: ∂T'(η) = T'(dη) = R'.action(dη) = ∫_{M ∩ B_{t₀}} F dHⁿ. The set {x : |x| < t₀} = B_{t₀} is open, hence measurable. So Measure.restrict_restrict gives ∫_{{|x| < t₀}} F dν = ∫_{B_{t₀} ∩ M} F dHⁿ = ∂T'(η).
3. (F is ν-integrable.) dη is a test form, so it is continuous with compact support K := tsupport(dη) ⊆ tsupport η ⊆ U (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). Hence b := sup_x |dη(x)| < ∞, since x ↦ |dη(x)| is continuous with compact support (covectorEuclideanNorm is continuous: a square root of a finite sum of squares of the continuous evaluations α ↦ α(e_I), continuous_eval_const; HasCompactSupport.comp_left with covectorEuclideanNorm_zero; Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). F is ν-a.e. strongly measurable for three reasons: θ is measurable; ξ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient); dη is continuous. The evaluation (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply with Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂). By (IC)(d), for ν-a.e. x, |F(x)| ≤ θ(x)·|dη(x)| ≤ b·θ(x)·1_K(x), because dη = 0 off K. Moreover ∫⁻ b·θ·1_K dν = ofReal(b)·∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞, by the IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult (K is compact and K ⊆ U). Hence F is ν-integrable: Integrable.mono' with the integrable bound 1_K·bθ (integrable_indicator_iff, using ν⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M) by Measure.restrict_restrict).
4. (Cut-offs.) For 0 < h < 1 apply (LC) with f := |·| (1-Lipschitz, lipschitzWith_one_norm), L := 1 and t := t₀. This gives a C^∞ function g_h : ℝ^P → ℝ with |g_h| ≤ 2 and ‖Dg_h(x)‖ ≤ 1/(h(1 − h/2)). Moreover Dg_h(x) ≠ 0 implies t₀ − h < |x| < t₀, g_h(x) = 1 if |x| ≤ t₀ − h, and g_h(x) = 0 if |x| ≥ t₀. For h ∉ (0, 1) put g_h := 0; these values never matter below. If g_h(x) ≠ 0 then |x| < t₀, so support g_h ⊆ B_{t₀}. Hence tsupport g_h ⊆ closure(B_{t₀}) ⊆ closedBall(0, t₀) ⊆ V (closure_mono, closure_ball_subset_closedBall, hypothesis).

Write S_h(t) := {x : t − h < f(x) < t} and N := μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}).
1. (Trivial cases.) If b ≤ a then Ioo a b = ∅ and the left side is 0. If L = 0, the hypothesis gives m(t) ≤ 0·(…) = 0 for every t ∈ (a, b) (in [0, ∞], 0·∞ = 0), so m = 0 a.e. for volume restricted to Ioo a b (ae_restrict_iff' with measurableSet_Ioo) and the left side is 0 (lintegral_mono_ae). If L > 0 and N = ∞, the right side is ∞. Assume from now on a < b and N < ∞.
2. (Distribution function.) For s ∈ ℝ let E_s := W ∩ {a < f < min(s, b)} and F(s) := (μ(E_s)).toReal. If s ≤ s' then E_s ⊆ E_{s'}, and μ(E_s) ≤ μ(E_b) = N < ∞; hence F is real valued and monotone on ℝ, ofReal(F(s)) = μ(E_s), F(s) = 0 for s ≤ a (then E_s = ∅) and F(b) = N.toReal.
3. (Strip estimate.) Let t ∈ (a, b) and 0 < h < t − a. E_t = W ∩ {a < f < t} is the disjoint union of W ∩ {a < f ≤ t − h} and W ∩ S_h(t), and W ∩ S_h(t) is measurable (W and f are measurable). By additivity (measure_union), μ(E_t) = μ(W ∩ {a < f ≤ t − h}) + μ(W ∩ S_h(t)) ≥ μ(E_{t−h}) + μ(W ∩ S_h(t)), because E_{t−h} = W ∩ {a < f < t − h} ⊆ W ∩ {a < f ≤ t − h} (note t − h < b). All terms are finite, so μ(W ∩ S_h(t)) ≤ ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) and ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ S_h(t)) ≤ ofReal((F(t) − F(t − h))/h).
4. (Differentiation.) F is monotone, so by Lebesgue's theorem (Monotone.ae_differentiableAt) it is differentiable at a.e. t ∈ ℝ. Let t ∈ (a, b) be such a point. By hasDerivAt_iff_tendsto_slope, (F(s) − F(t))/(s − t) → deriv F t as s → t, s ≠ t; with s = t − h and h → 0+ this says (F(t) − F(t − h))/h → deriv F t, hence ofReal((F(t) − F(t − h))/h) → ofReal(deriv F t). By step 3 (valid for all h ∈ (0, t − a), i.e. eventually in 𝓝[>]0), liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ S_h(t)) ≤ ofReal(deriv F t), and by hypothesis m(t) ≤ L·ofReal(deriv F t). Thus m(t) ≤ L·ofReal(deriv F t) for a.e. t ∈ (a, b).

By lintegral_mono_ae (valid for arbitrary, not necessarily measurable, functions) for volume restricted to Ioo a b, and lintegral_const_mul' (L ≠ ∞), ∫⁻_{(a,b)} m ≤ ∫⁻_{(a,b)} L·ofReal(deriv F t) dt = L·∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv F t) dt. deriv F ≥ 0 everywhere (Monotone.deriv_nonneg) and deriv F is integrable on [a, b] (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv), so ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv F) = ofReal(∫_{(a,b)} deriv F) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal), and ∫_{(a,b)} deriv F = ∫_{(a,b]} deriv F = ∫_a^b deriv F (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le) ≤ F(b) − F(a) = N.toReal (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc, uIcc a b = [a, b], F(a) = 0). Hence ∫⁻_{(a,b)} m ≤ L·ofReal(N.toReal) = L·N, since N < ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: Dispose of b ≤ a, L = 0 and μ(W ∩ {a<f<b}) = ∞.
F(s) := μ(W ∩ {a < f < min(s, b)}).toReal is monotone and μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) ≤ F(t) − F(t−h) for t ∈ (a, b), 0 < h < t − a.
At a.e. t (Lebesgue: monotone F is differentiable a.e.) the liminf is ≤ F'(t), so m(t) ≤ L·F'(t) a.e. on (a, b).

subproblems.title: Calculus of integer multiplicity representations: tangent locality, restriction, differences, orientation bound (reused accepted cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub)
subproblems.statement: (a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) if and only if M' does. (b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm).

Part (b), the restriction of an IMRep to a Borel set, is used by truncate (T′ = T⌞B_{t₀}). Part (d), |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| a.e. on the carrier, is used by action_bound and by boundary_mass (integrability). The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–160); Ch. 6, Remarks 3.2(1) and 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 287–293, 755–768), stated in the book without proof; and Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 for the orientation bound. Hⁿ := μHE[n] throughout. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). The statement has four parts: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction of a representation to a Borel set, (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents, (d) the orientation bound |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|; U is open in (a)–(c).

Preliminaries.
(P0) Normalization: SimonGMT's density theorems are stated for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure); hence null sets, finiteness and densities transfer verbatim, and Hⁿ is Borel regular (every set has a Borel hull of the same measure).
(P1) Scaling: for every set A, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries). Hence for Borel A and bounded Borel f, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y).
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6, for the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ, cf. simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, lim_{r↓0} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet. For n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I) det(B_I), the sum over increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, A_I the n×n submatrix of columns I. Proof: the j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_k B_{jk}A_{·k}, so by multilinearity det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k_1,…,k_n} B_{1k_1}⋯B_{nk_n} det(A_{·k_1}, …, A_{·k_n}); terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the remaining tuples by their underlying increasing tuple I (k = I ∘ σ for a permutation σ) gives Σ_I det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j, I_{σ(j)}} = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I). (For n > P both sides are 0 — no increasing I, and rank ABᵀ < n.)
(P4) Orientation bound. If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal in ℝ^P and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm). Proof: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|(Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|, since AAᵀ = (⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) is the identity. For n = 0, |α(∅)| = |α|.
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' Q imply ζ' = ζ or ζ' = −ζ, and IsUnitOrientationOf (−ζ) Q holds whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).

(d) Orientation bound. By the orientation field of an IMRep, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| for all α. (No openness of U is needed.)

(a) Locality. Let U be open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and D := M' ∖ M.
1. For R ∈ ℕ let U_R := {x ∈ U : |x| < R, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/R} (U_R := {|x| < R} if U = ℝ^P). U_R is open, closure(U_R) is a compact subset of U, and U_R ↑ U. D_R := D ∩ U_R is Borel with Hⁿ(D_R) ≤ Hⁿ(M' ∩ closure(U_R)) < ∞. By (P2) there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_R such that every x ∉ D_R ∪ Z_R satisfies Hⁿ(D_R ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ) as r ↓ 0. Let Z := ⋃_R Z_R, and let Z' ⊇ Z be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0). Let x ∈ M ∖ Z'; choose R with x ∈ U_R and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{r₀}(x) ⊆ U_R. Then x ∉ D_R (as x ∈ M) and D ∩ B̄_r(x) = D_R ∩ B̄_r(x) for r < r₀, so Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0). For r < r₀/ρ the sets η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure, so the integrals below are genuine Bochner integrals. Since η_{x,r} is injective, η_{x,r}(M') is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(D), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞ r^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{rρ}(x)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
Hence for every f the two families of integrals have the same limit as r → 0⁺ or both have none; the condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q for every x ∈ M ∖ Z' and every Q; the exceptional set M ∩ Z' is null for Hⁿ⌞M. ∎

(b) Restriction. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in the open set U and E a Borel set. Define R' with carrier M ∩ E and the same mult θ and orient ξ.
1. Structure fields: M ∩ E is Borel and contained in U; countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and θ > 0 on M ∩ E; ∫_{M∩E∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Orientation: by (P6) and (a) applied to M ∩ E ⊆ M ⊆ U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E and all Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ E) x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. With the orientation field of R (Hⁿ-a.e. on M) this gives the orientation field of R'.
3. The current: A(ω) := ∫_{M∩E} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By (d), |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ |ω|_∞ θ 1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so the integrand is integrable; A is linear. If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U and uniform convergence of all derivatives, in particular |ω_j|_∞ → 0 since all norms on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors are equivalent), then |A(ω_j)| ≤ |ω_j|_∞ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ → 0. So A is a GeometricCurrentOn U n and R' represents A (IMRep.Represents, IMRep.action). ∎

(c) Differences. Let A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, be represented by R_A = (M_A, θ_A, ξ_A) and R_B = (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B).
1. (Borel versions and good points.) Choose Borel ξ̃_A, ξ̃_B equal to ξ_A, ξ_B Hⁿ-a.e. on M_A, resp. M_B (a.e. strong measurability; set them 0 off the carriers). Let G be the set of x ∈ M_A ∪ M_B such that: if x ∈ M_A, then ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x) and there is Q_A(x) with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_A x Q_A(x) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_A x) Q_A(x); the analogous condition for B if x ∈ M_B; and, for each pair (N, N') among (M_A ∩ M_B, M_A), (M_A ∩ M_B, M_B) with x ∈ N, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q for every Q. By the orientation fields of R_A, R_B, by (P6) and by (a), (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; let N₀ ⊇ (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0).
2. (Overlap.) Let x ∈ (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀. The approximate tangent space of M_A ∩ M_B at x exists and equals Q_A(x) and also Q_B(x) (the equivalences defining G and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique); so Q_A(x) = Q_B(x) and by (P5) ξ̃_B(x) = ε(x)ξ̃_A(x) with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}. subproblems.title: Smooth cut-off of a sublevel set of a Lipschitz function, gradient ≤ L/(h(1 − h/2)), supported in the strip (reused accepted cmcs_level_cutoff)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0, f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz, t ∈ ℝ and 0 < h < 1. Then there is a C^∞ function g : ℝ^P → ℝ such that |g(x)| ≤ 2 for all x; ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ L/(h(1 − h/2)) for all x (operator norm of fderiv ℝ g x); Dg(x) ≠ 0 implies t − h < f(x) < t; g(x) = 1 whenever f(x) ≤ t − h; and g(x) = 0 whenever f(x) ≥ t.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration cmcs_level_cutoff (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.slicing-a1.level_cutoff-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit 81485ceb96999b3c8eabac3c5b058488a2bdc059). It is reused with its identical frozen type: a whitespace-normalised comparison with `theorem Submission.cmcs_level_cutoff` in that commit matches. That commit's only sorry is the frozen root theorem GMT.Ch07.main_theorem, and it declares no axioms. Role here: It supplies the radial cut-offs g_h of step 9(a) of the parent proof. boundary_mass applies it with f = |·|, L = 1 and t = t₀. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 4.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 1378–1402: a cut-off γ∘f with γ = 1 below a, γ = 0 above b and |γ'| ≤ (1+ε)/(b − a), used with f^(σ) in place of f when f is only Lipschitz), and step 3 of the parent proof (ε := h²/8, smooth γ with |γ'| ≤ 1/(h − 4ε) = 1/(h(1 − h/2)), g_σ := γ∘f_σ). Departure: here the profile γ is piecewise linear and the smoothing (sibling cmcs_lipschitz_smoothing) is applied to γ∘f instead of to f; this produces one smooth function with the same constant L/(h(1 − h/2)), the same localisation of Dg and the same plateaus, without constructing a separate smooth profile.
1. (Parameters.) δ := h²/4. Since 0 < h < 1, h − 2δ = h(1 − h/2) > 0. Let σ := δ/(2(L + 1)) > 0; then 2Lσ = Lδ/(L + 1) < δ.
2. (Profile.) γ(s) := max(0, min(1, (t − δ − s)/(h − 2δ))) for s ∈ ℝ. Then 0 ≤ γ ≤ 1; γ(s) = 1 if s ≤ t − h + δ (then (t − δ − s)/(h − 2δ) ≥ 1); γ(s) = 0 if s ≥ t − δ. γ is Lipschitz with constant (h − 2δ)⁻¹, as the composition of the affine map s ↦ (t − δ − s)/(h − 2δ) (Lipschitz constant (h − 2δ)⁻¹) with the 1-Lipschitz clamp r ↦ max(0, min(1, r)). Hence G := γ∘f is Lipschitz with constant K := L·(h − 2δ)⁻¹ = L/(h(1 − h/2)) (LipschitzWith.comp), 0 ≤ G ≤ 1, G(y) = 1 when f(y) ≤ t − h + δ and G(y) = 0 when f(y) ≥ t − δ.
3. (Smoothing.) The sibling cmcs_lipschitz_smoothing applied to G, K and σ gives a C^∞ function g : ℝ^P → ℝ with ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ K = L/(h(1 − h/2)) for all x, |g(x) − G(x)| ≤ K·σ for all x, and g(x') = c whenever G = c on B_σ(x'). This gives smoothness and the gradient bound.
4. (|g| ≤ 2.) K·σ = Lδ/(2(L + 1)(h − 2δ)) ≤ δ/(2(h − 2δ)) = h²/(8h(1 − h/2)) = h/(8(1 − h/2)) < 1/4, because h < 1 and 1 − h/2 > 1/2. Hence |g(x)| ≤ |G(x)| + K·σ ≤ 1 + 1/4 ≤ 2.
5. (Lower plateau.) Let f(x) ≤ t − h. For x' ∈ B_σ(x) and y ∈ B_σ(x') we have ‖y − x‖ < 2σ, so f(y) ≤ f(x) + L‖y − x‖ ≤ t − h + 2Lσ < t − h + δ and G(y) = 1. By the locality in step 3, g(x') = 1 for every x' ∈ B_σ(x). Thus g = 1 on the open ball B_σ(x), so g(x) = 1 and Dg(x) = 0 (g agrees near x with a constant: Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq and fderiv_const).
6. (Upper plateau.) Let f(x) ≥ t. For x', y as in step 5, f(y) ≥ f(x) − L‖y − x‖ ≥ t − 2Lσ > t − δ, so G(y) = 0; hence g = 0 on B_σ(x), so g(x) = 0 and Dg(x) = 0.
7. (Transition strip.) If Dg(x) ≠ 0, then by steps 5 and 6 neither f(x) ≤ t − h nor f(x) ≥ t, i.e. t − h < f(x) < t. Steps 3–7 give all the claimed properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take δ = h²/4, the piecewise-linear profile γ (1 below t − h + δ, 0 above t − δ, slope (h − 2δ)⁻¹) and G = γ∘f, which is L/(h(1 − h/2))-Lipschitz.
Smooth G at scale σ = δ/(2(L+1)) with cmcs_lipschitz_smoothing: gradient bound, |g − G| ≤ 1/4, locality.
If f(x) ≤ t − h (resp. f(x) ≥ t), G ≡ 1 (resp. 0) on B_{2σ}(x), so g ≡ 1 (resp. 0) on B_σ(x) and Dg(x) = 0.
Hence Dg(x) ≠ 0 forces t − h < f(x) < t.

subproblems.title: Leibniz rule d(gη) = g dη + dg ∧ η (reused accepted cmcs_cd_extDeriv_smul_leibniz)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) (x : Euclid P), DifferentiableAt ℝ g x → DifferentiableAt ℝ η x → exteriorDerivative (fun y => g y • η y) x = g x • exteriorDerivative η x + ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x))

This child is the comparator-accepted declaration cmcs_cd_extDeriv_smul_leibniz (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.slicing-a1.cutoff_defect-a1.leibniz-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit 19f5e1986c50f3aea0edcade3d15ca618e3f6763). That commit's only sorry is the frozen root theorem GMT.Ch07.main_theorem, and it declares no axioms. Role here: It is the Leibniz rule of step 9(b) of the parent proof, behind Simon's identity 4.11. cutoff_estimate uses it to identify d(gη) − g dη with dg ∧ η. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.11 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1378–1386). Its middle step T(γ∘f dω) − T(d(γ∘f ω)) = −T(γ'(f) df ∧ ω) rests on the Leibniz expansion d(γ∘f·ω) = γ∘f·dω + d(γ∘f) ∧ ω. This is step 1 (Leibniz rule) of the parent proof of cmcs_cutoff_defect_bound, isolated for an arbitrary function g and an arbitrary k-form η that are differentiable at the point x.

Notation: A := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin. For a k-form θ : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) k (DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k), SimonGMT's exteriorDerivative θ is an abbreviation (abbrev) of Mathlib's extDeriv θ, and Mathlib defines extDeriv θ x := A (fderiv ℝ θ x).

1. (Unfold the definitions.) By the two definitions just recalled, exteriorDerivative (fun y => g y • η y) x is definitionally A (fderiv ℝ (fun y => g y • η y) x), and exteriorDerivative η x is definitionally A (fderiv ℝ η x). So the claim is definitionally the equation
   A (fderiv ℝ (fun y => g y • η y) x) = g x • A (fderiv ℝ η x) + A ((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x)).
   In Lean, change the goal to this form with `show`.
2. (Product rule.) Let hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g x and hη : DifferentiableAt ℝ η x be the two hypotheses. Mathlib's product rule for a scalar function times a vector-valued function, fderiv_fun_smul hg hη, gives
   fderiv ℝ (fun y => g y • η y) x = g x • fderiv ℝ η x + (fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x).
   Here (fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x) is the continuous linear map v ↦ (fderiv ℝ g x v) • η x.
3. (Linearity of A.) A is the continuous linear map alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ applied to its argument. So A is additive: A (F + G) = A F + A G (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_add). It also commutes with real scalars: A (c • F) = c • A F (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul, used with c = g x).
4. (Conclusion.) Rewrite the left side of the goal of step 1 by step 2, then by the additivity of step 3, and finally by the homogeneity of step 3 at c = g x:
   A (g x • fderiv ℝ η x + (fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x)) = A (g x • fderiv ℝ η x) + A ((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x)) = g x • A (fderiv ℝ η x) + A ((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x)).
   This is the right side of the goal. In Lean, after the `show` of step 1, `rw [fderiv_fun_smul hg hη, ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_add, ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul]` closes the goal (checked against Mathlib 25730c7c). ∎
proof_key_steps: Unfold exteriorDerivative = extDeriv: exteriorDerivative θ x is definitionally alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv ℝ θ x); reduce the goal with `show`.
Product rule fderiv_fun_smul hg hη: fderiv ℝ (fun y => g y • η y) x = g x • fderiv ℝ η x + (fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (η x).
alternatizeUncurryFin is additive and ℝ-homogeneous (alternatizeUncurryFin_add, alternatizeUncurryFin_smul); rewriting with both closes the goal.

subproblems.title: Coefficient norm of a wedge with a 1-form: |β ∧ γ| ≤ ‖β‖·|γ| (reused accepted cmcs_wedge_norm_le)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let β : ℝ^P → ℝ be a continuous linear functional with operator norm ‖β‖ and γ a k-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) k). Let β ∧ γ be the (k+1)-covector ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (β.smulRight γ), i.e. (β ∧ γ)(v_0, …, v_k) = Σ_{i=0}^{k} (−1)^i·β(v_i)·γ(v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_k). Then |β ∧ γ| ≤ ‖β‖·|γ|, where |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm is the Euclidean coefficient norm |α| = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(m−1)})²)^{1/2} of an m-covector α (e the standard basis of ℝ^P).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (β : Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ) (γ : Covector (Euclid P) k), covectorEuclideanNorm (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (β.smulRight γ)) ≤ ‖β‖ * covectorEuclideanNorm γ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration cmcs_wedge_norm_le (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.slicing-a1.wedge_norm-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit 6c9a0741ef7348ef9dcc005b9eeaa2593511c6ca). It is reused with its identical frozen type: a whitespace-normalised comparison with `theorem Submission.cmcs_wedge_norm_le` in that commit matches. That commit's only sorry is the frozen root theorem GMT.Ch07.main_theorem, and it declares no axioms. Role here: It is the pointwise bound of step 9(d) of the parent proof, here without the factor √(m+1) of the parent. cutoff_estimate uses it as |dg ∧ η| ≤ ‖Dg‖·|η|. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: fact (E1) of the parent proof (|β ∧ γ| ≤ |β||γ|, proved there by rotating β to a multiple of a basis vector), with Simon's wedge product (Ch. 6, 1.1–1.3, chapter-06.txt lines 26–60) and Euclidean norm (1.15, line 178). We use the sibling regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis, denoted (Σ): for every m ∈ ℕ, every m-covector α and every orthonormal basis f = (f_0, …, f_{P−1}) of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P, Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = m!·|α|², where f∘j := (f_{j(0)}, …, f_{j(m−1)}).
Put ω := alternatizeUncurryFin (β.smulRight γ). By alternatizeUncurryFin_apply and (β.smulRight γ)(v) = β(v)·γ, for every v : Fin (k+1) → ℝ^P we have ω(v) = Σ_{i : Fin (k+1)} (−1)^i·β(v_i)·γ(Fin.removeNth i v).
1. (Riesz representative.) Let b := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Euclid P)).symm β. Then β(v) = ⟨b, v⟩ for every v (toDual_symm_apply) and ‖b‖ = ‖β‖ (toDual is a linear isometry equivalence).
2. (Case b = 0.) Then β = 0, so β.smulRight γ = 0 and ω = 0 (alternatizeUncurryFin is the continuous linear map alternatizeUncurryFinCLM, which maps 0 to 0). Hence |ω| = 0 ≤ ‖β‖·|γ| (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero, |γ| ≥ 0). From now on b ≠ 0; then ℝ^P ≠ {0}, so P ≥ 1 and 0 ∈ Fin P.
3. (An orthonormal basis adapted to b.) Let u := ‖b‖⁻¹·b, so ‖u‖ = 1, and let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ. Let R := reflection (ℝ ∙ (e_0 − u))ᗮ, a linear isometry equivalence of ℝ^P; since ‖e_0‖ = 1 = ‖u‖, R(e_0) = u (reflection_sub). The family f := e.map R (OrthonormalBasis.map), f_i = R(e_i), is an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P with f_0 = u. By orthonormality β(f_i) = ⟨b, f_i⟩ = ‖b‖·⟨f_0, f_i⟩, which equals ‖b‖ for i = 0 and 0 for i ≠ 0.
4. (Values on basis tuples.) Let j : Fin (k+1) → Fin P; note Fin.removeNth i (f∘j) = f∘(Fin.removeNth i j). By step 3, ω(f∘j) = ‖b‖·Σ_{i : j(i) = 0} (−1)^i·γ(f∘(Fin.removeNth i j)).
(a) If j is not injective, then f∘j is not injective (f is injective), so ω(f∘j) = 0 because ω is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective).
(b) If j is injective, at most one index i has j(i) = 0, so the sum has at most one term and ω(f∘j)² = ‖b‖²·Σ_{i : j(i) = 0} γ(f∘(Fin.removeNth i j))².
Hence in all cases (∗) ω(f∘j)² ≤ ‖b‖²·Σ_{i : Fin (k+1)} [j(i) = 0]·γ(f∘(Fin.removeNth i j))², since in case (a) the left side is 0 and the right side is a sum of squares.
5. (Summation.) Summing (∗) over all j : Fin (k+1) → Fin P and exchanging the finite sums, Σ_j ω(f∘j)² ≤ ‖b‖²·Σ_{i : Fin (k+1)} Σ_{j : j(i) = 0} γ(f∘(Fin.removeNth i j))². For fixed i, j ↦ Fin.removeNth i j is a bijection from {j : Fin (k+1) → Fin P | j(i) = 0} onto Fin k → Fin P with inverse j' ↦ Fin.insertNth i 0 j' (Fin.removeNth_insertNth, and Fin.insertNth_self_removeNth together with j(i) = 0). So the inner sum equals Σ_{j' : Fin k → Fin P} γ(f∘j')² = k!·|γ|² by (Σ) with m = k. Therefore Σ_j ω(f∘j)² ≤ ‖b‖²·(k+1)·k!·|γ|² = (k+1)!·‖b‖²·|γ|².
6. (Conclusion.) By (Σ) with m = k+1 and α = ω, Σ_j ω(f∘j)² = (k+1)!·|ω|². Hence (k+1)!·|ω|² ≤ (k+1)!·(‖b‖·|γ|)², and since (k+1)! > 0, |ω|² ≤ (‖b‖·|γ|)². Both |ω| and ‖b‖·|γ| are nonnegative (covectorEuclideanNorm is a square root), so |ω| ≤ ‖b‖·|γ| = ‖β‖·|γ| (sq_le_sq₀: for nonnegative reals a² ≤ c² ↔ a ≤ c). ∎
proof_key_steps: Write β = ⟨b, ·⟩ with ‖b‖ = ‖β‖; the case b = 0 is trivial.
Choose an orthonormal basis f with f_0 = b/‖b‖ (reflection of the standard basis), so β(f_i) = ‖b‖δ_{i0}.
On basis tuples, (β∧γ)(f∘j)² ≤ ‖b‖² Σ_i [j(i) = 0] γ(f∘removeNth i j)² (non-injective tuples give 0).
Summing and using removeNth/insertNth bijections and the basis-invariant square sum (Σ) twice gives (k+1)!|β∧γ|² ≤ (k+1)!‖b‖²|γ|².

subproblems.title: Dominated convergence for level cut-offs: ∫ g_h F dμ → ∫_{f<t} F dμ as h → 0+ (reused accepted cmcs_smp_cutoff_integral_tendsto)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, F : ℝ^P → ℝ μ-integrable, f : ℝ^P → ℝ measurable, t, C ∈ ℝ, and g : ℝ → (ℝ^P → ℝ).
